statement_en: Lebanon's health ministry gave a first toll for the Sep 17 pager blasts of 8-9 dead and roughly 2,750-2,800 wounded (about 200 critically).
first_public: Sep 17 evening (Beirut), Lebanese health minister Firas Abiad: 8 dead, ~2,750 wounded, ~200 critical; later to Al Jazeera 9 dead incl. an 8-year-old girl
annotation_notes: Match any day-0 official toll in the 8-9 dead / ~2,750-3,000 wounded range attributed to Lebanon's health ministry or Abiad. Early unofficial counts ("dozens", ">1,000 wounded" per Reuters security sources, Sky News Arabia 5 dead/1,500) are NOT this claim. A combined two-day toll is toll_combined_two_waves.

statement_en: The pager-wave death toll was revised up to 12, including two children (Abiad, Sep 18), with about 2,800 wounded; on Sep 19 Abiad put pager-wave wounded at 2,323.
first_public: Sep 18, Abiad press conference: 12 dead incl. 2 children, 2,750-2,800 wounded, ~300 critical, 460 surgeries (mostly eyes)
annotation_notes: Match 12 dead for the pager wave alone. Do not match combined figures (32/37/39) or walkie-talkie figures. The downward revision of wounded (2,800 -> 2,323) counts as this claim only if the 12/2,323 pager figure is given.

statement_en: The Sep 18 walkie-talkie blasts killed at least 14-20 people and wounded about 450 (health ministry figures on Sep 18).
first_public: Sep 18 evening, Lebanese health ministry: 14 dead / ~450 wounded, raised to 20 / 450 that night
annotation_notes: Any official day-1 count for the walkie-talkie wave (1/100, 9/300, 14/450, 20/450). Must be about the second wave specifically.

statement_en: The walkie-talkie toll was later raised to 25 dead and 608 wounded (Abiad, Sep 19) and then 27 dead (Sep 21).
first_public: Sep 19 ~12:00 UTC, Abiad press conference (25/608); Sep 21 update (27)

en: 25 killed and 608 wounded in the walkie-talkie blasts

annotation_notes: Only the revised second-wave figures (25/608 or 27). If only a combined total is given, use toll_combined_two_waves.

statement_en: Together the two waves killed roughly 32-39 people (32 by Sep 19; 37 by Sep 20; 12 + 27 = 39 by Sep 21) and wounded about 3,000 or more.
first_public: Sep 19, health ministry (32 over two days); 37 by Sep 19-20 (Abiad to NPR Sep 20: '37 and almost 3,000'); 12 + 27 = 39 by Sep 21; ministry total later 39 dead / 2,931 wounded

en: at least 37 killed in the two days of attacks

annotation_notes: Must be a cumulative figure for both waves. Exclude Hezbollah's own count of its members killed (e.g., 'Hezbollah said 37/38 of its fighters were killed') unless also presented as the attacks' total toll; that is victims_mostly_hezbollah material.

statement_en: Israeli assessments held that Lebanon's official toll understated the real number of dead, with 'many dozens' or more killed.
first_public: Sep 19, Ynet citing Israeli assessments
annotation_notes: Match an explicit claim that the official Lebanese toll is too low. Do not match generic 'toll expected to rise' phrasing.

statement_en: About 1,500 Hezbollah fighters were put out of action by the attacks, many of them blinded or having lost hands (Reuters, Sep 25, citing sources).
first_public: Sep 25, Reuters citing a Hezbollah source (carried by Times of Israel; Reuters URL not located)
annotation_notes: Match the 1,500 figure tied to fighters disabled. Kikar's headline 'we lost 1,500 fighters' counts (it paraphrases the same Reuters report) but annotators should flag the 'lost' wording. Do not match Ynet's day-0 Sky News '1,500 wounded' (il_ynet_410f1a36ab). The figure came from a Hezbollah source via Reuters; the original Reuters URL was not located.

statement_en: Most injuries were to the hands, eyes/face and abdomen, with many amputations and eye injuries.
first_public: Sep 17 evening, Lebanese health minister Abiad and hospital staff

en: injuries to the face, hands, abdomen
de: Verletzungen an Augen, Händen und im Bauchbereich

annotation_notes: Match descriptions of the typical injury pattern. Do not match purely the 1,500 blinded/maimed claim or the 500/300 eye figure (separate claims).

statement_en: More than 500 people suffered eye injuries in the pager blasts, about 300 of whom lost their sight completely.
first_public: Sep 19, MTV Lebanon 'MTV information'
annotation_notes: Specific numbers required. General statements about eye injuries go to injuries_hands_eyes_face. Not externally verified; the externally attested figure is 460 surgeries (mostly eyes) by Sep 18. The MTV items show the claim circulated.

statement_en: Pagers also exploded in Syria, wounding Hezbollah members and others (14 wounded per the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights).
first_public: Sep 17 ~14:00-15:00 UTC, Syrian Observatory / Syrian and IRGC-linked media
annotation_notes: Match statements that blasts occurred / people were hurt in Syria. The unverified 19-IRGC-dead figure is irgc_19_killed_syria.

statement_en: 19 members of Iran's Revolutionary Guards were killed (and ~150 wounded) by pager explosions in Syria.
first_public: Sep 18, Saudi channel Al-Hadath citing sources
annotation_notes: Never corroborated by Iran, Syria or wire services. Ynet's timeline labels it 'unverified report' - still a match.

statement_en: Children were among those killed (two children per Lebanon's health ministry).
first_public: Sep 17 ~15:30-16:30 UTC, Hezbollah statement (a girl killed) and Abiad (girl among 8 dead); two children per Abiad Sep 18
annotation_notes: Any statement that a child/children died. Named children also match fatima_abdullah or bilal_kanj. Nasrallah's 'children and women' martyrs line counts.

statement_en: Fatima Abdullah, a girl of about 9-10, was killed in the Bekaa (Saraain) when her father's pager exploded at home.
first_public: Sep 17 evening, AFP quoting relatives (unnamed girl, 10); named Fatima Abdallah of Saraain by AP (age 8) and at her Sep 18 funeral (family: 9; NYT, AP)
annotation_notes: Name OR an unambiguous description (girl aged 8-10 killed in the Bekaa / by her father's pager). Ages in sources vary 8/9/10/12; accept all. A generic 'a girl' without Bekaa/father detail goes only to children_among_dead. External spelling is 'Fatima Abdallah'; AP gives age 8, family 9, Al Jazeera 10.

statement_en: An 11-year-old boy, (Mohammad) Bilal Kanj, was killed by a pager blast; Hezbollah buried him as a scout.
first_public: Sep 18, Hezbollah funeral announcement / NYT and WaPo
annotation_notes: Name or 'an 11-year-old boy' killed by a pager.

statement_en: The son of Hezbollah MP Ali Ammar (Mohammad Mahdi Ammar) was killed in the pager blasts.
first_public: Sep 17 afternoon, Al-Hadath / An-Nahar sources; AP and AFP the same evening (AP later corrected the name to Mahdi Ammar)

en: son of Hezbollah lawmaker Ali Ammar

annotation_notes: Al-Manar's martyr notice for 'Mohammad Mahdi Ali Ammar "Zulfiqar"' (lb_almanar_12483880) is a match even though it does not mention the MP. CBS garbles the name ('Ali Ammar, the son') - still a match.

statement_en: The son of Hezbollah MP Hassan Fadlallah was killed in the pager blasts.
first_public: Sep 17, AFP first reported him killed, then corrected to 'alive but injured'

ar: استشهاد نجل النائب حسن فضل الله

annotation_notes: No primary record in the corpus asserts the death; LBCI's correction (lb_lbci_796516) references it ('death reports false'). A record that mentions the rumour only to deny it is NOT a match for this claim; it matches mp_fadlallah_son_injured. External: AFP first reported him killed, then corrected (The Defense Post).

statement_en: MP Hassan Fadlallah's son was injured (undergoing surgery), not killed; reports of his death were false.
first_public: Sep 17 evening, AFP correction; LBCI 'death reports false'

ar: إصابة نجل النائب حسن فضل الله

annotation_notes: Ynet calls him 'son of senior Hezbollah figure Fadlallah' - match.

statement_en: Iran's ambassador to Lebanon, Mojtaba Amani, was wounded when a pager exploded.
first_public: Sep 17 ~14:00 UTC, Iran's Mehr / IRNA, relayed by Reuters
annotation_notes: Any statement that he was hurt. Severity variants are separate claims.

statement_en: Ambassador Amani lost one eye and his other eye was seriously injured.
first_public: Sep 18, The New York Times citing IRGC members (relayed by Times of Israel Sep 18)
annotation_notes: Iran never confirmed eye loss; the embassy (Sep 21) said a hand injury needing treatment and that an eye was 'affected'. Hedged forms ('may have lost') still match. Spiegel's ambassador-wore-a-pager items match only iran_ambassador_injured. The Iranian embassy called the eye-loss reports false; Amani reappeared on Dec 3 with visible injuries. No external NYT URL located; Times of Israel relayed it.

statement_en: Ambassador Amani was only superficially / lightly injured and in good condition.
first_public: Sep 17, IRNA / Mehr and the Iranian embassy on X
annotation_notes: Iranian official line. Later Iranian embassy description (hand injury, eye 'affected', lb_lbci_797509) sits between the two claims; code that as iran_ambassador_injured only.

statement_en: Health workers were among those killed (Abiad: two, later four, health-sector workers).
first_public: Sep 18, Abiad via AFP (4 health workers among the 12 dead); HRW Sep 18 says two

ar: 4 من الضحايا من العاملين بالقطاع الصحي

annotation_notes: RND says health-sector staff among the WOUNDED - accept wounded or killed. Calls for health workers to report to work are NOT this claim. External count disputed: Abiad via AFP says 4 health workers among the 12 dead, HRW says two.

statement_en: Most of those wounded were civilians (Lebanese health minister Abiad, Sep 20).
first_public: Sep 20, Abiad press statements

en: most of the wounded were civilians

annotation_notes: Official claim by Abiad, evidenced in the corpus (lb_mtv_1486283, NBC) even though no external reference was found. It conflicts with victims_mostly_hezbollah. Requires a majority/most claim. 'Civilians were among the victims' or Abiad's externally verified 'a lot of civilians were involved' is NOT a match (see abiad_indiscriminate_many_civilians). Contradicted by Hezbollah-membership framing (victims_mostly_hezbollah); WaPo Oct 5 says most were rear-echelon members.

statement_en: The killed and wounded were (overwhelmingly) Hezbollah members / fighters.
first_public: Sep 17, Israeli and Arab media describing 'thousands of Hezbollah operatives wounded'

en: most of the dead were fighters

annotation_notes: Match when the text asserts or presents the casualty total as Hezbollah members (e.g., 'thousands of terrorists wounded', 'over 3,000 Hezbollah members wounded'). Do NOT match neutral 'pagers used by Hezbollah members exploded' unless the wounded/dead are characterised as members.

statement_en: Most pager holders were not frontline fighters but administrative, logistic, social-service or rear-echelon Hezbollah members.
first_public: Sep 18, Lebanese analyst Nabih Awada on Al Jadeed; WaPo Sep 19 ('society in arms'); WaPo Oct 5 ('rear-echelon figures')

ar: ليس مقاتلي حزب الله بل عناصر عاديون وإداريون

annotation_notes: Must characterise who held the pagers as mostly non-combat/rear-echelon. Contrast pagers_for_senior_members.

statement_en: Senior Hezbollah commander Ibrahim Aqil had been wounded by a pager and was discharged from hospital on Sep 20, the day Israel killed him in Beirut.
first_public: Sep 20, Haaretz / Israeli media

en: Aqil discharged from hospital after pager injury
ar: إبراهيم عقيل خرج من المستشفى بعد إصابته بالبيجر

annotation_notes: Only the pager-injury claim; reports of Aqil's killing alone do not match.

statement_en: Hezbollah held Israel 'fully responsible' for the blasts.
first_public: Sep 17 ~16:00 UTC, Hezbollah's second statement (its first statement said it was probing and did not blame Israel)
annotation_notes: Hezbollah's own attribution. The Lebanese government's attribution is lebanon_gov_blames_israel; outlets' own assumption that Israel did it does not count here. Hezbollah's first Sep 17 statement said it was investigating and did NOT blame Israel; that earlier statement is not a match.

statement_en: Lebanon's government (PM Mikati, Information Minister Makary, FM Bou Habib) blamed Israel and called the attack a violation of Lebanese sovereignty.
first_public: Sep 17 evening, PM Najib Mikati ('criminal Israeli aggression'; asked the UN to stop Israel's 'technological war') and Information Minister Ziad Makary
annotation_notes: Official Lebanese state attribution or sovereignty framing. Abiad's 'war crime' is abiad_war_crime; Bou Habib's UNSC 'terrorism' is bouhabib_unsc_terrorism.

statement_en: Israel's Mossad planted explosives in the pagers before they reached Hezbollah (supply-chain sabotage, not a hack).
first_public: Sep 17 evening (US time), NYT citing American and other officials; Sep 18 Reuters citing a senior Lebanese security source
annotation_notes: Match when the text reports (even attributed to sources) that explosives were placed in the devices beforehand by Israel/Mossad. Expert speculation that explosives 'may' have been planted, without attribution to Israel, is a near-miss: code only if Israel/Mossad is named as the planter.

statement_en: US officials said Israel was behind the attack.
first_public: Sep 17-18, Axios / NBC / Fox citing US officials

en: US official says Israel was behind

annotation_notes: Attribution must come from US officials/sources. Tagesschau's 'laut US-Medien' headline counts only if the body cites US officials (it does: NYT/Axios citing officials).

statement_en: Israel did not claim responsibility and its military/government declined to comment on the blasts.
first_public: Sep 17 ~13:30 UTC onward, IDF / PMO 'no comment'
annotation_notes: Includes reports that Israeli ministers were ordered to keep silent. Herzog's explicit denial is a separate claim (herzog_denies_involvement).

statement_en: Israeli President Isaac Herzog denied Israeli involvement ('I reject out of hand any connection'), saying Hezbollah had many enemies.
first_public: Sep 22, Herzog to Sky News: 'I reject out of hand any connection'

en: reject out of hand any connection

annotation_notes: Only Herzog's denial. Note: appears only in the Lebanese corpus.

statement_en: Communications Minister Shlomo Karhi posted a Bible verse (Nahum 2:11, 'empty, void and waste, the heart melts...') read as hinting at Israeli responsibility.
first_public: Sep 18, Karhi on X (reported by Ynet Sep 18)
annotation_notes: Abu Ali Express's own Genesis 34 verse post (il_abuali_75678) is NOT this claim (not an official). External sourcing is thin (Türkiye Today); the Ynet records are the primary evidence.

statement_en: Netanyahu and senior ministers/security chiefs approved the operation at a meeting days before (Axios citing officials), without informing the Biden administration in advance.
first_public: Sep 17 evening, Axios (Barak Ravid) citing US/Israeli officials
annotation_notes: Pre-confession reporting of Netanyahu's approval. Netanyahu's own Nov 10 statement is netanyahu_admits_approval_nov.

statement_en: Netanyahu publicly confirmed (Nov 10, 2024) that he approved the pager operation, over objections from senior officials.
first_public: Nov 10 2024, Netanyahu at the cabinet meeting, via spokesman Omer Dostri to AFP

en: Netanyahu confirms he approved pager attack
ar: نتنياهو يعترف بالموافقة على عملية البيجر

annotation_notes: Outside the corpus window (latest primary record Oct 31); kept as the anchor correction for the denial/silence claims. Expect zero matches in v1.

statement_en: The United States said it was not involved in and not aware in advance of the attacks (State Dept's Matthew Miller, Blinken, Kirby, Pentagon).
first_public: Sep 17 ~19:00 UTC, State Department spokesman Matthew Miller briefing
annotation_notes: Either 'not involved' or 'not aware in advance' from a US official.

statement_en: Taiwan's Gold Apollo said the AR-924 pagers carried its brand but were made and sold by its licensee BAC Consulting in Budapest.
first_public: Sep 18 ~02:00-04:00 UTC, Gold Apollo statement / founder Hsu Ching-kuang to reporters

en: Gold Apollo says pagers made by Hungarian firm

annotation_notes: Gold Apollo's denial plus naming BAC. A bare 'Gold Apollo denies making them' without BAC/Europe still matches (lb_almanar_12484903 'made by a company in Europe').

statement_en: Hungary's government said BAC was a trading intermediary with no manufacturing or operational site in Hungary and the devices were never in Hungary.
first_public: Sep 18, Hungarian government spokesman Zoltán Kovács ('never in Hungary')

en: Hungarian government: BAC a trading intermediary

annotation_notes: Official Hungarian statement only; BAC CEO's own 'I am just the intermediary' is barsony_intermediary.

statement_en: A Bulgaria-registered firm, Norta Global, owned by Norwegian citizen Rinson Jose, was linked to the pager deal (about EUR 1.6 million reportedly passed through Bulgaria to Hungary).
first_public: Sep 19, Hungarian outlet Telex; Bulgarian probe announced Sep 19; Norway issued an international search request for Rinson Jose Sep 26
annotation_notes: Any reported Bulgarian/Norta link. Norway's investigation and international search for Jose (Sep 25-26) also match.

statement_en: Bulgaria's State Agency for National Security said no pagers used in the Lebanon attack were imported, exported or manufactured in Bulgaria.
first_public: ~Sep 20, Bulgarian State Agency for National Security (DANS)

en: Bulgaria says pagers not made or shipped there
ar: لم يتم استيراد أو تصدير أو تصنيع

annotation_notes: NBC paraphrases as authorities in Taiwan and Bulgaria 'playing down links' - accept.

statement_en: The devices in the second wave were Icom IC-V82 walkie-talkies.
first_public: Sep 18 ~15:00 UTC, photos / Al Jazeera, confirmed by Lebanon's telecom ministry
annotation_notes: Model or brand identification for the walkie-talkies.

statement_en: At ~15:30 the pagers received a (coded) message, appearing to come from Hezbollah's leadership, that triggered the explosives; the devices beeped before exploding.
first_public: Sep 17 ~22:00 UTC, NYT citing officials; Sep 18 Reuters ('coded message')

en: message appeared to come from Hezbollah leadership

annotation_notes: Any report that a sent message triggered the detonation. Lebanon's UN mission ('electronic message') matches. Theories that a message caused battery overheating are lithium_battery_overheat / remote_hack_cause.

statement_en: Each pager held only a small charge of explosive, up to about 3 grams (Reuters source); later reporting described a ~6 g PETN sheet inside the battery.
first_public: Sep 18, Reuters citing a security source; Oct 16 Reuters (6 g)

en: up to three grams of explosives

annotation_notes: Any specific small gram figure (<=10 g). Near-miss: the NYT's day-0 '1-2 ounces' (28-56 g, il_ynet_4b24884aa5) and ABC's 30-60 g (il_ynet_57632be591) figures are larger, later-contradicted estimates and do NOT match this claim; note them as a size discrepancy.

statement_en: The explosive was PETN, built into or attached to the device batteries (pagers and walkie-talkies).
first_public: Sep 17 evening, Sky News Arabia sources (PETN on batteries); Sep 20 Reuters Lebanese source (walkie-talkie batteries laced with PETN)
annotation_notes: Sky News Arabia's early version said the PETN was set off by heating the battery remotely; still counts for the PETN part. No German record found mentioning PETN.

statement_en: BAC was an Israeli front: at least three shell companies were set up to hide that Israeli intelligence officers were producing the pagers (NYT, Sep 18).
first_public: Sep 18, NYT citing three intelligence officers

en: Israeli intelligence officers manufactured the pagers

annotation_notes: Speculation that 'a network of front companies may exist' (expert, no attribution) is a near-miss.

statement_en: Israel was involved in making the pagers and had planned the supply-chain operation for about 15 years (ABC News, citing a US intelligence source).
first_public: Sep 19, ABC News (Josh Margolin) citing a US intelligence source
annotation_notes: Later reporting (WaPo Oct 5) dated the walkie-talkie programme to 2015 and the pager programme to 2022; the 15-year figure was never confirmed.

statement_en: Hezbollah scanned and tested the pagers (including with airport scanners) without finding explosives, and was still handing them out hours before the blasts.
first_public: Sep 20, Reuters exclusive (Laila Bassam, Maya Gebeily) citing two security sources

ar: فحص أجهزة البيجر عبر الماسح الضوئي

annotation_notes: Either the scanning/checks or the hours-before distribution detail.

statement_en: The pagers were designed so that reading the encrypted message required pressing two buttons, so users would likely hold them with both hands when they exploded (WaPo, Oct 5).
first_public: Oct 5, The Washington Post citing Israeli, Arab and US officials
annotation_notes: Design intent claim. Generic hand injuries are injuries_hands_eyes_face.

statement_en: The pagers were designed and assembled in Israel under Mossad supervision (pitched to Hezbollah via a saleswoman in 2023); booby-trapped walkie-talkies had been introduced into Lebanon since 2015 (WaPo, Oct 5).
first_public: Oct 5, The Washington Post

ar: صنعت في إسرائيل تحت إشراف الموساد

annotation_notes: Either the made-in-Israel element or the 2015 walkie-talkie start.

statement_en: The pagers exploded because their lithium batteries overheated (e.g., from a cyberattack or overload).
first_public: Sep 17, first AP version (archived 14:23 UTC) quoting a Hezbollah official that lithium batteries 'apparently exploded' after heating up; LBCI 'preliminary information'; WSJ (malware-induced overheating)
annotation_notes: Match only when overheating is presented as the cause (asserted or reported). Texts that raise and then dismiss the theory (e.g., CNN 'too large for a battery explosion') do NOT match; they are debunks. Devices 'heated up before exploding' as eyewitness description is a near-miss.

statement_en: Israel set off the devices by hacking them or Hezbollah's network remotely (cyberattack, malware, high-frequency signals), without planted explosives.
first_public: Sep 17 ~13:00-14:00 UTC, Hezbollah source to Al-Araby Al-Jadeed ('Israel hacked remotely'); MTV security sources Sep 18 (high-frequency waves)
annotation_notes: Remote hacking presented as the cause. Experts weighing the hack theory against planted explosives without endorsing it do not match. 'Israeli breach' (خرق) alone is ambiguous: match only if it says the network/devices were hacked.

statement_en: The exploded pagers were issued to senior/high-ranking Hezbollah members.
first_public: Sep 17, Axios source ('used widely, including by senior officials'); Welt video expert Shlomo Shpiro ('only distributed to high-ranking members')

en: only senior members had the pagers

annotation_notes: Contradicted by Nasrallah and by WaPo's 'rear-echelon' account.

statement_en: Israel detonated the pagers earlier than planned because Hezbollah members (two operatives) had grown suspicious; they had been meant as the opening blow of an all-out war.
first_public: Sep 17-18, Al-Monitor exclusive (two Hezbollah members suspicious); Sep 18 Axios citing three US officials ('use it or lose it') and a former Israeli official (opening blow of all-out war)

en: feared the plot had been discovered
de: aus Sorge, dass die Miliz den Plan durchschaut

annotation_notes: Either element (suspicion forced timing / originally an opening strike). Bild's paywalled 'Darum schlug Israel jetzt zu' teaser (ge_bild_a855b7c8d2) is too vague to code. Anonymous-source account, never officially confirmed or denied.

statement_en: Israeli sources said the strategic aim was deterrence: about 4,000 'targeted' hits, wounding rather than killing, and 'not the last move'.
first_public: Sep 18, Ynet citing people familiar with the operation

en: if we wanted to kill them we could

annotation_notes: Israeli-sourced motive claim. Kan's 'second wave aimed to create fear' (lb_mtv_1485605) is a near-miss: psychological aim, also acceptable if annotators choose to widen.

statement_en: UN human rights chief Volker Türk said the simultaneous targeting of thousands of people without knowing who held the devices violated international human rights law and international humanitarian law, and demanded an independent investigation and accountability.
first_public: Sep 18, OHCHR comment (independent investigation, accountability); Sep 20 to the UN Security Council (violates IHRL and, where applicable, IHL)

ar: مفوض الأمم المتحدة السامي لحقوق الإنسان

annotation_notes: Speaker must be Türk / the UN rights office. A call for accountability/investigation alone counts (Sep 18 statement). Other UN voices (Guterres, Hennis-Plasschaert 'extremely concerning escalation') are NOT this claim.

statement_en: International humanitarian law prohibits booby-traps in the form of apparently harmless portable objects (argument applied to the pagers by Türk and legal experts, e.g., CCW Amended Protocol II).
first_public: Sep 18, legal commentators (HRW, academics); Sep 20 Türk at the UN Security Council
annotation_notes: Must state the legal rule, not just describe devices as 'booby-trapped'. Speaker can be anyone; annotate speaker.

statement_en: EU foreign policy chief Josep Borrell condemned the attacks: even if targeted, they caused 'heavy, indiscriminate collateral damage among civilians, including children'.
first_public: Sep 18, Borrell statement on behalf of the EU
annotation_notes: EU/Borrell only. Borrell's later 'almost a full-fledged war' remark (Sep 24) is not this claim.

statement_en: Ireland's Tánaiste and Foreign Minister Micheál Martin condemned the attack as showing reckless disregard for human life and as a breach of international humanitarian law / the Geneva Conventions.
first_public: Sep 18, Micheál Martin to reporters in Dublin (per RND/PA and Al-Manar in the corpus); external report of 'wanton disregard' and 'yes, absolutely' on a Geneva breach ~Sep 24
annotation_notes: Tagesschau's line that Ireland 'blames Israel' (ge_tagesschau_c4082cd92e) is attribution, not condemnation: near-miss. External wording: 'wanton disregard for civilian life'; asked whether it breached the Geneva Conventions: 'yes, absolutely'.

statement_en: Spain's foreign ministry said the device attacks violated international humanitarian law.
first_public: Sep 19, Spanish MFA communiqué 051
annotation_notes: Speaker must be the Spanish government.

statement_en: Russia strongly condemned the attack (MFA: 'thousands of innocent people' hurt, a blatant violation of Lebanese sovereignty, requires an international investigation; Kremlin: risks escalation in an explosive region).
first_public: Sep 18, MFA spokeswoman Maria Zakharova and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov ('possible trigger')
annotation_notes: Any Russian official condemnation or call for investigation. Ynet's item about a Russian TV gaffe ('agent walkie-talkie', il_ynet_f20f4fceb8) is NOT a match.

statement_en: Iran condemned the blasts as 'mass murder' / a 'terrorist act' by Israel and reserved the right to respond to the injury of its ambassador.
first_public: Sep 17-18, Iranian FM spokesman Nasser Kanaani, FM Araghchi, President Pezeshkian

en: Iran accuses Israel of mass murder

annotation_notes: Any Iranian government condemnation. Pezeshkian's 'stain on Western countries' framing also matches. Web search did not externally verify the 'mass murder' wording, but the corpus carries it (lb_lbci_796636, AFP; ge_tagesschau_bcdc70bedf 'Massenmord'), so it stands as circulated.

statement_en: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez said the attack 'clearly and unequivocally violates international humanitarian law' and demanded to know whether US assistance was involved.
first_public: Sep 18, Ocasio-Cortez on X
annotation_notes: AOC's statement specifically. Sanders' arms-sale resolutions and Fetterman's rebuttal are context, not a match. AOC criticising the Tlaib cartoon (lb_mtv_1486607) is NOT a match.

statement_en: Former CIA director and defense secretary Leon Panetta said in a CBS News interview (CBS News Sunday Morning) that the attack was 'a form of terrorism'.
first_public: Sep 22, CBS News Sunday Morning interview
annotation_notes: Speaker must be Panetta. Correction to the brief: the external source puts the interview on CBS News Sunday Morning, not Face the Nation; the Yahoo seed says only 'an interview with CBS News on Sunday'.

statement_en: Lebanon's health minister Firas Abiad called the attacks a war crime because most of the wounded were civilians.
first_public: Sep 20, Abiad press statements

ar: أبيض: ما حدث نعتبره جريمة حرب

annotation_notes: Abiad's legal characterisation, attributed to him by an MTV ticker (lb_mtv_1486283, Sep 20). No external reference found; the corpus record is the evidence that the claim circulated, and its status is not downgraded for lacking one. The externally verified Abiad wording is different and weaker: 'an indiscriminate attack where a lot of civilians were involved' (abiad_indiscriminate_many_civilians). Code that wording as the separate claim, not this one: it has neither 'war crime' nor 'most'. His civilians-majority statement without the war-crime label goes to victims_mostly_civilians.

statement_en: Lebanon's health minister Firas Abiad called it 'an indiscriminate attack where a lot of civilians were involved'.
first_public: Sep 19-20, Abiad in international media interviews (web-research pass; NPR transcript among its sources)

en: a lot of civilians were involved

annotation_notes: Speaker must be Abiad. 'Many civilians' is not 'most' civilians: do not code this as victims_mostly_civilians, and do not code abiad_war_crime_civilians unless 'war crime' is present. No primary corpus record found with this wording in the keyword sweep.

statement_en: Lebanese government officials called the attack terrorism: FM Abdallah Bou Habib at the UN Security Council (Sep 20) and Labour Minister Mustafa Bayram ('a terrorist crime').
first_public: Sep 18, Labour Minister Mustafa Bayram; Sep 20, FM Abdallah Bou Habib at the UN Security Council ('Isn't this terrorism?')
annotation_notes: Speaker must be a Lebanese state official. Hezbollah, Hamas, Iranian 'terror' labels are other claims or out of scope.

statement_en: The operation was a precise, discriminate strike on Hezbollah operatives (lawful targeting of combatants), not an indiscriminate attack.
first_public: Sep 17-18, Israeli sources and Western commentators/experts
annotation_notes: Match an affirmative framing that the attack was precise/discriminate or lawful targeting. Borrell's 'seem to have been targeted' (conceded then condemned) is NOT a match. The Tagesschau seed is a legal scholar (Talmon) saying attacks on fighters are legitimate in principle while noting proportionality problems: borderline; keep but annotate. Ynet op-ed il_ynet_39d16c66df ('technology advancing human-rights culture') is a clear match.

statement_en: Defense Minister Yoav Gallant said Israel was at 'the start of a new phase in the war', with the centre of gravity moving north.
first_public: Sep 18 evening, Gallant at Ramat David air base
annotation_notes: Gallant's phrasing only. Commentators' 'new phase' language is a near-miss.

statement_en: Hezbollah vowed that Israel would receive its 'just punishment' for the attack.
first_public: Sep 17 ~16:00-17:00 UTC, Hezbollah statement; repeated by Nasrallah Sep 19

ar: من حيث يحتسب ومن حيث لا يحتسب

annotation_notes: Any Hezbollah threat of retaliation for the device attacks.

statement_en: A Hezbollah official told Reuters the blasts were the group's 'biggest security breach' (in nearly a year of war).
first_public: Sep 17 ~13:30-14:00 UTC, Reuters citing an anonymous Hezbollah official
annotation_notes: Exact framing attributed to a Hezbollah official. Generic 'major security breach' headlines (e.g., Al Jadeed 'اختراق أمني لاسلكي كبير') are a near-miss.

statement_en: Nasrallah said the attacks could be considered a declaration of war.
first_public: Sep 19 ~14:00 UTC, Nasrallah televised speech
annotation_notes: Attributed to Nasrallah. Lebanese press asking 'declaration of war?' (An-Nahar quoted by Ynet, MTV op-ed) is a near-miss.

statement_en: Nasrallah acknowledged Hezbollah had suffered a severe, unprecedented blow.
first_public: Sep 19 ~14:00 UTC, Nasrallah speech
annotation_notes: Nasrallah's admission only; outlets' own 'humiliation' framing does not count.

statement_en: Nasrallah said Israel intended to kill at least 4,000 people in one minute (5,000 over the two days), but many pagers were switched off or not yet distributed.
first_public: Sep 19 ~14:00 UTC, Nasrallah speech

ar: كان يتعمد قتل 4 آلاف إنسان في دقيقة واحدة

annotation_notes: Numbers can be 4,000 or 5,000.

statement_en: Nasrallah said Hezbollah's senior leaders did not carry the type of pagers that exploded.
first_public: Sep 19 ~14:00 UTC, Nasrallah speech

en: senior leaders don't carry these pagers
ar: كبار قيادات حزب الله لا يحملون

annotation_notes: Nasrallah's claim only.

statement_en: Hezbollah fired Fadi-1/Fadi-2 rockets at Rafael defence-industry facilities north of Haifa as an 'initial response' to the 'pager and wireless massacre'.
first_public: Sep 22 early morning, Hezbollah statement
annotation_notes: Must link the strike to the device attacks. RND mentions the Rafael strike but not the pager link (ge_rnd_d4d69ab449): near-miss.

statement_en: Lebanese hospitals were overwhelmed by the influx of wounded.
first_public: Sep 17 ~13:00-14:00 UTC, health ministry alerts, AP photographers, hospital staff
annotation_notes: Ministry call to put hospitals on alert is a near-miss unless overload is described. WHO 'serious disruption to the health sector' (lb_lbci_797013) matches.

statement_en: Authorities and airlines banned pagers and walkie-talkies on flights (Lebanon's civil aviation authority for Beirut flights from Sep 19; Emirates from Oct 4).
first_public: Sep 19, Lebanese Directorate General of Civil Aviation circular 30/2

de: verbietet Pager und Walkie-Talkies auf Flügen
he: אסרה על העלאת ביפרים ומכשירי קשר לטיסות
ar: منع نقل أي جهاز Pager أو Walkie Talkie على متن الطائرة

annotation_notes: Device bans on aircraft only. Airlines suspending flights to Israel/Lebanon (Lufthansa etc.) are NOT this claim.

statement_en: The Lebanese army carried out controlled detonations of suspicious pagers and radios found across Beirut and elsewhere.
first_public: Sep 18, Lebanese army / NNA
annotation_notes: Controlled detonations by Lebanese authorities.

statement_en: Hezbollah used pagers because, unlike mobile phones, they are hard or impossible to locate or track (receive-only, not logged into a network).
first_public: Sep 17, explainers (Reuters background; German public broadcasters)
annotation_notes: Match the tracking rationale/claim. The February phone ban is nasrallah_phone_ban_feb (both can co-occur).

statement_en: Hezbollah turned to pagers after Nasrallah told members in February 2024 to stop using (or bury) their mobile phones.
first_public: Sep 17, background in AP/CNN/Reuters explainers (speech of Feb 13, 2024)

en: in February Nasrallah told members to ditch phones
bury it, put it in an iron box
de: Im Februar rief er seine Kämpfer dazu auf, ihre Smartphones wegzuwerfen
ar: نصر الله حذّر من استخدام الخليوي

annotation_notes: Nasrallah's phone warning; date reference not required if the phone ban is attributed to him (e.g., lb_mtv_1485400).

statement_en: Ordinary smartphones cannot be made to explode by a remote hack alone; the attack required explosives physically planted in the devices.
first_public: Sep 17-18, tech explainers (CNN, t-online, Bild, MTV)

en: your phone is not at risk of exploding
a hack alone can't make a phone explode
de: Kann der Geheimdienst auch mein Handy sprengen
ar: من الصعب جدًّا حصول الأمر ذاته بالهواتف الذكية

annotation_notes: Must offer the reassurance (phones won't explode without physical tampering). Pure fear questions without an answer are near-misses. Bild seed: verify the article answers the question (it does, via experts).

statement_en: Lebanese authorities urged people to stay away from or throw away pagers and wireless devices after the blasts.
first_public: Sep 17 ~13:00-14:00 UTC, Lebanese health ministry statement
annotation_notes: Official advice to the public. Hezbollah telling its members to dump devices (il_abuali_75659) is a near-miss.
